hook.line: Sundays at the café are slow, and Vale has nobody to talk to. English says *bored* and *boring* with nearly the same word, and mixing them up is how you end up telling people you are a dull person.
hook.es: Los domingos me aburro en el café.
hook.en: On Sundays I get bored at the café.

examples.es: Me aburro cuando no hay clientes.
examples.en: I get bored when there are no customers.

examples.es: Hoy no hay clientes y estoy aburrida.
examples.en: There are no customers today and I'm bored. (a woman speaking)
Do you get bored at home? (to a friend)

examples.es: Hernando no es aburrido, es muy simpático.
examples.en: Hernando isn't boring, he's very nice.

rule:
English has two words, *bored* and *boring*. Spanish uses the verb to tell them apart.

*Me aburro*: I get bored. Something happens to you: *Me aburro los domingos*.
*Estoy aburrido*: I'm bored right now. Use *aburrida* if you are a woman.
*Es aburrido*: it is boring, a quality of the film or the person: *Esta película es aburrida*.

So *estoy* tells how you feel, and *es* tells what something is like. The adjective matches whoever it describes.

Soon you will also meet *esta serie me aburre*, where the cause comes first.
smallPrint: Teachers call *aburrirse* a pronominal verb: the *se* version is the one where you are the one who feels it.

options: Do you get bored at home?

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (I get bored on Sundays): ___ los domingos. (Me aburro / Soy aburrido)
yourTurn.why: Something happens to you, so *me aburro*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (This film is boring): Esta película ___ aburrida. (es / está)
yourTurn.why: Boring is what the film is like, so *es*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish (a man speaking): I'm bored right now.
yourTurn.why: How you feel right now is *estoy*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish (a woman speaking): I'm bored right now.
Ask a friend if they get bored at home.
yourTurn.why: *Te* is your friend, and the verb ends in *-es* for *you*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about Hernando: Me aburro los domingos.
Type in Spanish: That series is very boring.
yourTurn.why: Boring describes the series, so *es* and *aburrida*.

pitfalls.why: *Soy aburrido* says you are a boring person; for how you feel, use *estoy*.
Without *me* the verb means you bore other people; to get bored yourself, add *me*.
A film does not feel bored; it is boring, so *es*.

personal: Tell us when you get bored, or one thing that is boring. Use *me aburro* or *es aburrido*.
